newsitem.title: UK: Cowie bus unit drives profits up 48 pct.
newsitem.headline: Cowie bus unit drives profits up 48 pct.

text.p: Cowie Group Plc Plc, the transport to retail combine, reported a 48 percent rise in half year pre-tax profits on Thursday, driven by its enlarged bus division.

Pre-tax profits for the six months to June 30 rose to 47.6 million pounds ($77.8 million), with turnover up 33 percent to 702 million pounds. The half year dividend payout was 3.6 pence, a rise of six percent on the previous year. Summing up the outlook, Gordon Hodgson, chief executive, said the new government's focus on creating an integrated transport system meant "we are in a strong position to progress."

"We are positioned to benefit strongly from the opportunities presented in all our markets," said Hodgson in the results statement. "..and we are pursuing a number of expansion possibilities for our vehicle management and bus operations both in the UK and mainland Europe."

The group said its vehicle management unit was also making progress in winning "substantial outsourcing contracts" with top British companies and its motor retailing network continued to develop profitably. Demand for British cars in August, when the licence registration prefix changes to 'R', is also expected to reach near-record levels according to industry estimates.

Looking at a divisional breakdown of the results, Cowie's bus division contributed 49 percent of profit after tax and 232 million in turnover. It is now the second largest operator in Britain, with 18 percent market share after acquiring British Bus last year.
Cowie is currently seeking to expand further and is also in talks with local authorities to increase its partnership agreements.

The finance division, largely comprising of vehicle management, saw turnover up 16 percent to 136 million. The motor division saw a 19 percent rise in profit to 7.6 million and turnover of 335 million.
